anchor_as_quoted: This is the center of the Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the earliest surviving extended works of literature.

detail: The further-reading section offers five scholarly and museum sources (George, Spar, ETCSL, British Museum Flood Tablet, Freeman) but no Wikipedia link for the Epic of Gilgamesh, which has a substantial Wikipedia article that would serve as the standard entry-point for a listener wanting to look up the work.

anchor_as_quoted: Written Mesopotamian flood stories predate the final form of the biblical Genesis account, and scholars study how stories circulated, changed, and acquired new meanings over time.
claim: The lecture asserts that written Mesopotamian flood narratives predate the final form of Genesis and that their relationship is a matter of scholarly study.
detail: The registered sources are centered on the Gilgamesh flood tablet and its rediscovery, not on the dating of Genesis or the comparative transmission of flood traditions, so a source on Genesis dating and Mesopotamian flood-text chronology would be needed.
anchor: Written Mesopotamian flood stories predate the final form of the biblical Genesis account, and scholars study how stories circulated, changed, and acquired new meanings over time.

adjudication.note: Covered in scope: gilgamesh-george is the standard critical edition whose front matter (registered kind scholarly_textual_history) treats the textual tradition and the Genesis comparison; the sentence is hedged general scholarly framing, not a dated claim. Adjudicated from title/kind/notes plus standard scholarship; sandbox has no network to re-fetch the PDF.

Fix: register a provenance or heritage-history source for the Nineveh/Rassam acquisitions, or soften the sentence to what the collection page actually states. Low severity; non-blocking.
